_comment: Wording taken from 'Year 6 Science — Unit 8: Food Preservation Technology'. Exam sentences are verbatim. Do not paraphrase them.

learn.name: Learn
learn.brief: Food spoils because microorganisms grow on it. Send each food to the station that stops them.

practice.name: Practice
practice.brief: Two more stations are open, and the cold cabinet now has two settings. The food no longer tells you which method it needs — look at what the food is.

panic.name: Panic
panic.brief: Every station is running and food is spoiling faster. Keep the microorganisms down.

recall.name: Recall
recall.brief: The station labels are gone and the machines have moved. Recognise each one by how it works.

why.name: Why It Works
why.brief: After every preservation you must say what the method changes.

mastery.name: Mastery
mastery.brief: The stations have swapped places. Nothing is where you left it — you have to know the methods themselves.

newmachines.name: Two More Machines
newmachines.brief: Smoking dries food with smoke — the same reason drying works. Canning kills microorganisms with heat, then seals the food in. Keep the fire going, and turn the lid until it is airtight.

wholekitchen.name: The Whole Kitchen
wholekitchen.tagline: Every machine. No labels. A question every time.
wholekitchen.brief: Eight machines, no name plates, and they move while you work. You know all of this now — show it.

removes_water.long: Water is removed, so microorganisms cannot grow easily.

removes_air.long: Air is removed, so microorganisms cannot reproduce easily.

low_temperature.long: Low temperature slows down the growth of microorganisms.

changes_environment.long: High acidity or a high concentration of sugar or salt prevents microorganisms from growing.

seals_surface.long: The surface is coated so microorganisms cannot grow on it.

heat_then_cool.long: Heat kills the microorganisms, then the food is cooled immediately at 4°C.

drying.name: Drying
drying.explain: Drying removes water from food. Microorganisms cannot survive or become inactive when there is no water.
drying.exam: Drying preserves food by removing water, so microorganisms cannot grow easily.
drying.hint: Hang it up and let the sun take the water out.
drying.instruction: Hang the food on a hook, then sweep the sun across it.
drying.recallClue: Sun and air, no water left
drying.detail: Food can be dried under the sun or in an oven.

freezing.name: Freezing
freezing.explain: Food is stored at 0°C and below. Low temperature makes microorganisms less active and slows down their growth.
freezing.exam: Freezing and cooling preserve food because low temperature slows down the growth of microorganisms.
freezing.hint: Put it inside and set it to 0°C or below.
freezing.instruction: Open the door, put the food in, close it, then set the dial.
freezing.recallClue: Cold air, frost on the door
freezing.detail: Freezing stores food at 0°C and below. Examples: chicken, meat, prawns, squid.
freezing.dialWrong: Not the right temperature for this food.

cooling.name: Cooling
cooling.explain: Food is stored at a low temperature, around 4°C. Low temperature makes microorganisms less active and slows down their growth.
cooling.exam: Freezing and cooling preserve food because low temperature slows down the growth of microorganisms.
cooling.hint: Put it inside and set it to about 4°C.
cooling.instruction: Open the door, put the food in, close it, then set the dial to 4°C.
cooling.recallClue: Cold air, frost on the door
cooling.detail: Cooling stores food at a low temperature, around 4°C. Examples: fruits, vegetables, milk.
cooling.dialWrong: Not the right temperature for this food.

vacuum.name: Vacuum Packing
vacuum.explain: Vacuum packing removes air from food packaging. Microorganisms cannot reproduce without air inside the packaging.
vacuum.exam: Vacuum packing preserves food by removing air so microorganisms cannot reproduce.
vacuum.hint: Bag it, then pull all the air out.
vacuum.instruction: Hold the pump until the air gauge reaches zero, then seal.
vacuum.detail: The bag is sealed so no air can get back in.

pickling.name: Pickling
pickling.explain: High acidity or high concentration of sugar or salt prevents microorganisms from growing.
pickling.exam: Pickling preserves food because vinegar, sugar or salt prevents the growth of microorganisms.
pickling.hint: Into the jar, then pour a solution over it.
pickling.instruction: Drop the food in, tilt a bottle to fill the jar, then twist the lid shut.
pickling.detail: Pickling means soaking food in vinegar, sugar solution or salt solution.
pickling.anySolutionOk: All three work — vinegar, sugar solution and salt solution all stop microorganisms.

salting.name: Salting
salting.explain: Salt removes moisture from food and prevents microorganisms from growing.
salting.exam: Salting preserves food by removing moisture from food.
salting.hint: Cover it with a lot of salt.
salting.instruction: Scoop salt, then rub it all over the food until it is covered.
salting.recallClue: A heap of salt being rubbed in
salting.detail: Salting means covering food with a large quantity of salt.

pasteurising.name: Pasteurising
pasteurising.explain: Pasteurising uses heat to kill microorganisms without changing the taste or nutritional value of food.
pasteurising.exam: Pasteurising preserves food by heating it to kill microorganisms and then cooling it quickly.
pasteurising.hint: Heat it, then cool it straight away.
pasteurising.instruction: Hold HEAT until the programme completes, then hit COOL immediately.
pasteurising.recallClue: A hot pipe and a cold pipe
pasteurising.detail: Heat at 63°C for 30 minutes, or 72°C for 15 seconds. Then cool immediately at 4°C.
pasteurising.coolTooLate: Too slow — it must be cooled immediately.
pasteurising.eitherProgrammeOk: Both programmes work — 63°C for 30 minutes, or 72°C for 15 seconds.

boiling.name: Boiling
boiling.explain: Boiling uses high temperature to kill microorganisms such as bacteria and fungi.
boiling.exam: Boiling preserves food because high temperature kills microorganisms.

waxing.name: Waxing
waxing.explain: Waxing means coating fruits and vegetables with liquid wax. This prevents microorganisms from growing on the surface.
waxing.exam: Waxing preserves food by coating the surface and preventing microorganisms from growing.

smoking.name: Smoking
smoking.explain: Smoking dries food using smoke. This method takes a long time.
smoking.exam: Smoking preserves food by drying the food and reducing moisture.

canning.name: Canning and Bottling
canning.explain: Cooking food at high temperature to kill microorganisms and storing it in airtight cans or bottles.
canning.exam: Canning and bottling preserve food by killing microorganisms and sealing the food in airtight containers.

quiz.whichMethod: Which preservation method did we just use?

microbeA.low_temperature: They become less active and grow slowly
microbeA.high_temperature: They are killed by the heat
microbeA.changes_environment: They cannot grow in vinegar, sugar or salt
microbeA.heat_then_cool: They are killed by the heat, then kept out by the cold
microbeA.seals_surface: They cannot grow on a coated surface

spoilage.title: Food Spoilage
spoilage.what: Food spoilage means food has become bad and unsafe to eat.
spoilage.why: Food spoilage happens because of the action of microorganisms.
spoilage.grow: Bacteria and fungi grow easily on food that is moist, exposed to air, or not stored properly.
spoilage.unsafe: Spoilt food is unsafe for consumption.

senses.touch: Food changes texture, becomes slimy or soft

importance.title: Why preservation matters
items: Allows food to be eaten all year round
Makes food easier to store and transport

a11y.keyboardHelp: Use Tab to choose a food, then number keys 1 to 6 to send it to a station.
a11y.bookArea: Fact Book pages. Use the left and right arrow keys to turn the page.
